figure: FIGURE 3.4 (Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior) — caption, italic per-token line
issue: The caption states the challenger's 8-bit KV as '0.655 MB/token', but the correct value is 0.0655 MB/token (a 10x slip). This is internally inconsistent with the same caption's '~0.6 GB for the 9.2K input' and with the 32L / 8-KV-head / 128-dim shape.
evidence: Recompute from the shape the caption itself gives: per token per layer = 2 (K+V) x 8 KV heads x 128 head-dim x 1 byte (8-bit) = 2,048 B; x 32 layers = 65,536 B/token = 0.0655 MB/token (decimal). x 9,200 tokens = 602,912,000 B ≈ 0.60 GB, matching the red box 'MoE 0.6 GB' and the 20:1 ratio vs dense (1.31 MB/token -> 12 GB). The printed 0.655 MB/token x 9,200 = 6.03 GB, which contradicts the printed ~0.6 GB in the same sentence. The dense per-token (1.31 MB/token -> 12 GB) is consistent; only the challenger per-token is off by 10x.
acceptance_test: Caption reads '0.0655 MB/token (challenger 32L/4096H GQA)' and 0.0655 MB/token x 9.2K equals ~0.6 GB, consistent with the red box and with the 20:1 per-token ratio (1.31 : 0.0655) matching the 12 GB : 0.6 GB total ratio.

figure: FIGURE 3.4 — right column legend and per-token line
issue: The symbol '11.4' denotes two different quantities in the figure body: GB-per-expert in the legend ('inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)', 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)') but billion-params-per-TWO-experts in the per-token line ('11.4B top-2'). The per-expert param count (5.7B) appears only in the caption, not the figure, so a reader cannot reconcile the two 11.4s from the figure alone.
evidence: Legend: 6 x 11.4 = 68.4 ≈ 68 GB and 2 x 11.4 = 22.8 ≈ 23 GB, so 11.4 = GB per single expert (= 5.7B params x 2 B, FP16). Per-token line: '11.4B top-2 + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B', so 11.4B = params for two experts (= 2 x 5.7B). Caption confirms 'the two routed experts (~11.4B = 2 × 5.7B)'. The same numeric token 11.4 is therefore a per-expert GB value in one place and a per-two-expert param value in another, with the bridging 5.7B absent from the figure.
acceptance_test: The figure body explicitly states the per-expert values (e.g., '1 expert = 5.7B params ≈ 11.4 GB (FP16)') and the per-token line is written 'top-2 = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B)', so no single symbol carries two meanings and the legend's 6x/2x GB sums are verifiable from the figure alone.

figure: FIGURE 3.4 — right column expert grid (active vs inactive boxes)
issue: Grayscale distinguishability is weak between active experts (orange fill) and inactive experts (light-gray fill). The two fills map to close gray levels, so the 2-active / 6-inactive distinction relies on a subtle shade difference rather than a robust encoding.
evidence: Orange fill (≈ RGB 255,165,0) converts to ≈ 68% gray; the light-gray inactive fill (≈ RGB 211-230) converts to ≈ 83-90% gray. The ~15-20% gray gap is visible but borderline at print size; the only stronger cue is border weight (thick red on active vs thin gray on inactive), which also compresses in grayscale. The legend swatches share the same weak fills, so matching is by position, not by a high-contrast in-figure cue.
acceptance_test: In a pure-grayscale render, active vs inactive expert boxes are separable by a fill pattern (e.g., hatch on one class) or by a ≥20% gray-level difference or a clearly distinct border style, without relying on the orange-vs-light-gray hue.
